title: Pearson to acquire Workera in major push into AI skills and workforce assessment
key_facts: Pearson has agreed to acquire Workera, an AI-native skills intelligence platform used by enterprises and government bodies to measure workforce capabilities.
Workera uses agentic AI, psychometrics and adaptive assessment through role-specific scenarios and simulations.
Founded 2019, based in Palo Alto, about 60 employees; customers include ServiceNow, Accenture and the US Space Force.
The technology will sit inside Pearson's Enterprise Learning & Skills business once the deal closes.
Workera co-founder and CEO Kian Katanforoosh will join that business's leadership team after completion.
Pearson expects completion in the second half of 2026, subject to customary conditions including any regulatory approvals.
No price is given in the article.
quote_evidence: Pearson has agreed to acquire Workera, the AI-native skills intelligence platform used by enterprises and government organizations to measure and verify workforce capabilities.
Pearson says the acquisition is expected to complete in the second half of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions, including any required regulatory filings or approvals.
why_it_matters_hint: Employers want proof of what staff can do with AI, not just course completion.
notes: Price not disclosed in the article.
